description:
About me: CS student at Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute. Specializing in Machine Learning, Python (Pandas, LightGBM, ETL), and C# .NET Backend. I have experience applying ML to physical processes and building solid backend architectures.

What we are building: A working interactive simulator. We will train an ML model on NASA's combustion data and use SHAP to explain the physical factors driving fire risks in space, wrapped in a clean UI.
summary: FlameGap turns two decades of NASA microgravity combustion research into direct answers for crew fire safety. It summarizes 16 investigations from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository in one comparable format, ranks them for a chosen crewed environment and goal, and shows where the evidence stops. The key result: for the oxygen-enriched atmospheres planned for lunar habitats, none of the three safety pillars (prevention, detection, suppression) has direct evidence from real cabin materials, and real test data suggest that switching off ventilation may not put a fire out. An AI assistant answers questions from the study cards and names its sources.
details:
What it does. The user picks an environment (spacecraft, station, lunar or Mars base, pressurized rover, Earth). Mission brief shows evidence coverage per safety pillar and tests five common fire-safety assumptions against space experiments. Evidence gaps maps fuel type against oxygen level. Materials gives a passport per material across investigations. Test data plots 179 real ACME CFI-G tests: in still air at 18-24 % oxygen all 41 ignited flames went out on their own, while at 33-40 % a third (31 of 92) burned until the fuel was cut off. Ranking scores investigations with a transparent, adjustable formula for three goals taken from the challenge. Each study card shows our summary next to NASA’s original text, and Ask the data answers free-form questions.

How it works. Study cards were written from PSI pages, metadata and experimental tables. Scripts in the repository recheck the quoted facts against NASA’s metadata and recompute every table-derived number.

Benefits and goals. An engineer can see in minutes what is known, what is assumed and what was never tested. Next step: load metadata and tables directly from the PSI repository so new investigations appear automatically.

Limits. FlameGap summarizes published descriptions, abstracts and test tables; it does not analyze raw measurements. It covers 16 of the PSI combustion investigations.

Tools. Python, Streamlit, Plotly, pandas, Google Gemini API. No hardware. Code: github.com/ferumshtern/flamegap
projectRefs: Kim et al. 2023, Spherical gas-fueled cool diffusion flames
